items.followUp: How are cathode rays produced in a discharge tube?

rubric.why: Shows how the positive particles originate.
rubric.description: Gas atoms are ionized, producing positive ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that gas atoms lose electrons or become positive ions.

rubric.why: Identifies how the rays emerge from the tube.
rubric.description: The positive ions move towards the cathode and pass through its holes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the positive ions pass through the perforated cathode.

modelAnswer: Gas atoms in the discharge tube lose electrons and form positive ions.
These ions move towards the cathode and pass through its perforations, producing positive rays (canal rays).

items.followUp: Write the electronic configuration of a chlorine atom, atomic number 17.

rubric.why: Identifies the number of electrons in a neutral phosphorus atom.
rubric.description: A neutral phosphorus atom has 15 electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating or using the correct electron count.

rubric.why: Gives the correct arrangement of the electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct configuration.

modelAnswer: Phosphorus has atomic number 15, so a neutral phosphorus atom has 15 electrons.

rubric.why: Identifies organic chemistry as a branch of chemistry concerned with a defined subject.
rubric.description: Organic chemistry is a branch of chemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a branch of chemistry.

rubric.why: States the subject studied in this branch.
rubric.description: It deals with hydrocarbons and their derivatives.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning hydrocarbons and their derivatives, or an equivalent description of carbon compounds and their derivatives.

modelAnswer: Organic chemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with the study of hydrocarbons and their derivatives.

rubric.why: States the periodic relationship in the law.
rubric.description: The properties of elements are periodic functions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the properties recur periodically.

rubric.why: Gives the basis used in Mendeleev's law.
rubric.description: The periodicity is related to the atomic masses of the elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying atomic mass (or atomic weight) as the basis.

modelAnswer: Mendeleev's Periodic Law states that the physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic masses.

items.followUp: Describe the trend in atomic size across a period and down a group.

rubric.why: Gives the trend across a period.
rubric.description: Ionization energy generally increases from left to right across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct across-period trend.

rubric.why: Gives the trend down a group.
rubric.description: Ionization energy generally decreases down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct down-group trend.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy generally increases from left to right across a period.
Ionization energy generally decreases down a group.

items.followUp: Define electron affinity and name the halogen with the highest electron affinity.

rubric.why: Defines the attraction for bonding electrons.
rubric.description: Electronegativity is an atom's tendency to attract the shared pair of electrons in a bond towards itself.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining the tendency to attract shared or bonding electrons.

rubric.why: Identifies the element with the highest electronegativity.

modelAnswer: Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom in a molecule to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself.

items.followUp: Why do ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten?

rubric.why: Identifies the particles and forces holding an ionic solid together.
rubric.description: Ionic compounds contain oppositely charged ions held together by strong electrostatic forces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the strong attraction between oppositely charged ions.

rubric.why: Explains why high temperatures are needed to melt or boil the compound.
rubric.description: A large amount of energy is needed to overcome these forces and separate the ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that considerable energy is needed to overcome the ionic attractions.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds contain oppositely charged ions held together by strong electrostatic forces in a crystal lattice.
A large amount of energy is needed to overcome these forces and separate the ions, so ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points.

items.followUp: Define a polar covalent bond and give one example.

rubric.why: Distinguishes a non-polar covalent bond by how electrons are shared.
rubric.description: A non-polar covalent bond is formed when the bonding pair of electrons is shared equally between the bonded atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the electrons are shared equally.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of a non-polar covalent bond.
rubric.description: Examples include H₂, Cl₂, O₂ and N₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a correct example.

modelAnswer: A non-polar covalent bond is a covalent bond in which the bonding pair of electrons is shared equally between the bonded atoms.
Examples include H₂, Cl₂, O₂ and N₂.
